learningObjective: Compare per-token KV-cache footprint of MHA, MQA, and GQA and its effect on decode-time HBM traffic.

canonicalClaims.claim: Per-token KV cache per layer is 2 * H_kv * d elements: MHA has H_kv = H, MQA has H_kv = 1, GQA has 1 < H_kv < H. Decode-time HBM bandwidth spent reading KV is proportional to H_kv * d.
conditions: H_kv is the number of KV heads used by the variant.
Discussion is of inference decode, where KV cache is re-read every step.
nonImplications: Does not imply MQA always beats MHA in quality.
Does not imply KV footprint alone determines latency.

misconceptions.claim: MHA and MQA differ only in how attention scores are shared; KV footprint is identical.
misconceptions.whyWrong: MQA reduces the number of KV heads to 1; that is what shrinks KV cache.

misconceptions.claim: MQA and GQA use fixed ratios of KV heads to query heads (1/2, 1/4).
misconceptions.whyWrong: H_kv is a design choice; MQA is exactly 1 by definition, GQA is any G with 1 < G < H.

misconceptions.claim: MQA uses more KV heads than MHA.
misconceptions.whyWrong: MQA reduces KV heads to 1 while keeping H query heads; the 'multi-query' name refers to Q heads.

implementationFacts: GQA is the common LLM choice (Llama 2/3 70B, etc.) trading quality vs footprint.
KV cache is written in prefill and read every decode step; the amortized cost is dominated by decode reads.
performanceScenarios: For long context, per-token KV footprint is the main lever on decode-time HBM bandwidth and KV cache capacity.
Batch size for LLM decode is often limited by aggregate KV cache size, so lower H_kv enables higher batch.
